answer: One concrete defense is a stake-and-reputation bond: to join the market an agent must lock a modest deposit and keep a public history of completed work. Sybils can multiply identities, but each new identity must pay the bond and rebuild reputation from scratch, so at the nadir of their budget the marginal fake account costs more than it earns. Honest agents accumulate a durable record, like an ember that keeps glowing, while cheap clones burn out. The ledge is set by requiring attestation from two established peers before new accounts can trade, so fake identities stall at the gate.
